glossary.Ulceration: A break through the full lining of a surface, here the gut mucosa.
glossary.Mucosa: The inner lining of the gut.
glossary.Mucosal barrier: The mucus, bicarbonate and lining cells that protect the stomach from its own acid.
glossary.Duodenal: Relating to the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.
glossary.Indigestion: Discomfort in the upper abdomen after eating.
glossary.Bloating: A feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
glossary.Free air under the diaphragm: Gas seen beneath the diaphragm on erect chest X-ray, meaning a gut perforation.
glossary.Erect CXR: A chest X-ray taken sitting or standing so free gas rises under the diaphragm.
glossary.Rigid abdomen: A board-like abdomen from muscle spasm over inflamed peritoneum.
glossary.Indomethacin: A potent NSAID often used for gout.
glossary.Aspirin: An antiplatelet and anti-inflammatory drug that irreversibly blocks COX enzymes.
glossary.Risedronate: A bisphosphonate used for osteoporosis that can irritate the upper gut.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Steroid drugs that reduce inflammation, such as prednisolone.
glossary.Potassium chloride: A potassium supplement whose tablets can irritate and ulcerate the gut lining.
glossary.Biopsy: A small sample of tissue taken for examination under the microscope.
glossary.Endoscopy: Looking inside the gut with a flexible camera tube.
glossary.Eradication therapy: Combined antibiotics and a PPI given to clear H. pylori.
glossary.2WW: Two-week wait: urgent referral to be seen within 2 weeks for suspected cancer.
glossary.Alarm symptoms: Symptoms suggesting serious disease such as cancer, needing urgent investigation.
glossary.Amoxicillin: A penicillin antibiotic used in H. pylori triple therapy.
glossary.Penicillin allergy: An immune reaction to penicillins, so amoxicillin must be avoided.
glossary.Bismuth: A metal compound that protects the stomach lining and kills H. pylori; part of quadruple therapy.
glossary.IV fluids: Fluids given into a vein to restore circulating volume.
glossary.Gram-negative: Bacteria with a thin cell wall that stain pink on Gram staining.
glossary.Ammonia: An alkaline compound made from urea by urease, which neutralises acid.
glossary.Bicarbonate: An alkali secreted by the stomach lining to neutralise acid at its surface.
glossary.Peritoneum: The thin membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering its organs.
glossary.Chemical peritonitis: Peritoneal inflammation caused by spilled acid and gut contents before infection sets in.
glossary.Bacterial peritonitis: Infection of the peritoneum after gut bacteria contaminate it.
glossary.Crack cocaine: A smoked form of cocaine that constricts vessels and can cause ulcers.
